patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Saleor and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Saleor only if your buying job matches “Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3999/mo, En” rather than WooCommerce's shape. Choose WooCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPaymen” rather than Saleor's shape. Workflow advantage: Saleor leans shared coverage; WooCommerce leans catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Saleor and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Saleor is Headless GraphQL commerce — OSS self-host free; Cloud Select $1599/mo, Volume $3999/mo, Enterprise quote. Forever Free is non-commercial onl; WooCommerce is Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPayments processing are separate TCO lines..
- Company-size focus: Saleor (mid-market, enterprise) vs WooCommerce (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Saleor-leaning — vs WooCommerce-leaning catalog-management.
- Researched limits: Saleor — Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO; WooCommerce — You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS.

Limitations — Saleor: Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO; Forever Free Cloud is non-commercial — not a production merchant free plan; WooCommerce: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS; Extension sprawl can inflate TCO and maintenance.

Poor-fit cases: Saleor is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Cloud Select floor ($1599/mo) is high versus WooCommerce hosting TCO · WooCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS · Avoid Saleor if you actually need WooCommerce's motion (Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
